title: Injective component map for tensor quotients
statement: For a Noetherian finite algebra S over R, a prime p of R, and n>0, the quotient tensor product (R_p/m^n) tensor_R S admits an injective R-linear map to the product over primes q over p of the corresponding localized quotients, carrying pure tensors to localized products.

proof.text: Set A = R_p, m = its maximal ideal, B = A tensor_R S, and I = m^n B. Mathlib Algebra.TensorProduct.quotientTensorEquiv identifies (A/m^n) tensor_R S with B/I. For each q over p, construct the R-algebra map psi_q : B -> S_q by tensor-product lifting of Localization.localRingHom and S -> S_q. Ideal.map_map identifies I S_q with m^n S_q, so Ideal.quotientMapₐ induces g_q : B/I -> S_q/(m^n S_q). Compose the product of the underlying R-linear maps with the quotient-tensor equivalence to construct phi.

For each maximal ideal P of B, base-change finiteness (Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change) makes B finite, hence integral, over A. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-maximal-contracts-maximal], P contracts to a maximal ideal of A, necessarily m. Thus q = P intersect S is prime and contracts to p; this follows from the scalar-tower identities and IsLocalization.AtPrime.under_maximalIdeal.

B is a localization of S at the image of R minus p (Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorRight). Therefore B_P is a localization of S at q by IsLocalization.isLocalization_isLocalization_atPrime_isLocalization, giving the canonical S-algebra equivalence B_P -> S_q. Its composite with B -> B_P agrees with psi_q: IsLocalization.ringHom_ext reduces equality to S, where both maps are the structural localization map.

If psi_q(b) belongs to I S_q for every q over p, apply the preceding identification to every maximal ideal P of B. Transporting ideal membership along the equivalence B_P -> S_q shows b/1 belongs to I B_P. Then [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-membership-at-maximal-localizations] gives b in I.

If phi(x) = phi(y), represent the difference of their images in B/I by b in B. Each g_q kills the class of b, so psi_q(b) lies in I S_q. The preceding ideal-membership criterion gives b in I, hence equality in B/I and then x = y by injectivity of the quotient-tensor equivalence. The pure-tensor formula follows from quotientTensorEquiv_apply_tmul, quotientMapₐ on representatives and Algebra.TensorProduct.lift_tmul.

proof_origin.place: Quotient-product argument; K3 proves the required injectivity directly by the Mathlib maximal-localization criterion instead of Artinian decomposition.
